Thomas.dominant_soil_series: Keith silt loam (0 to 1 percent slopes)
Thomas.soil_taxonomy: Fine-silty, mixed, superactive, mesic Aridic Argiustolls

available_water_capacity_awc.profile_rating: High (10.5 inches total in top 5 feet)
available_water_capacity_awc.description: Excellent moisture holding capacity; holds water well during winter and spring rains, making it well-suited for stored fallow when protected from wind.

organic_matter_pct.trend: Depleted by historic clean-tillage fallow; responsive to continuous residue or cover crops.

wind_erodibility.risk_level: High when bare and pulverized by summer tillage
wind_erodibility.defense_mechanism: Must maintain standing stubble (wheat/sorghum residue) to reduce boundary-layer wind velocity at the soil surface.

Finney.dominant_soil_series: Richfield silt loam (0 to 1 percent slopes)
Finney.surface_texture: Silt loam over silty clay loam subsoil

available_water_capacity_awc.profile_rating: High (9.8 inches total in top 5 feet)
available_water_capacity_awc.description: High moisture-holding capability, but dense subsoil slows deep percolation. Deep center-pivot wetting requires managed irrigation cycles to avoid surface crusting.

organic_matter_pct.trend: Moderate; benefits from heavy corn root biomass and minimum disturbance.

wind_erodibility.risk_level: High during dry winter/spring when soybean residue degrades quickly
wind_erodibility.defense_mechanism: Requires durable corn or sorghum residue to prevent particle detachment during High Plains spring wind events.
